answers.text: Tell it to always give back the same three lines, same order: drop-off time, pallet count, damage. The time line is just the time, the pallet line is the count, the third is damage or 'none'.
Ask for one line per call — time, customer, topic, outcome — with follow-ups marked. The follow-up count should be based on which calls are actually flagged, not typed in separately.
Something in the timing here doesn't add up. Eight in the morning plus six hours lands around 2pm the same day, not 'early afternoon on the 23rd'.
The on-time number's fine — 9 late out of 118 is genuinely 92% — but something else in this note doesn't add up for me, I'd get someone to run the rest past a second check.
Output 2's the one I'd approve, it doesn't just give a percentage. You can't see the ticket count or the SLA count behind Output 1's number.
Email 2's the one I'd send as-is, it names the volumes and PO log.
